subject: Binned data in Distance for R

messages.author: 7f87f78f0cd24437
messages.subject: Binned data in Distance for R
parts:
Dear All,

 

I am just getting started with distance sampling. I am analysing some bird point count data, which was collected in binned distances. I have a question regarding the Distance in R package. According to the Miller et al. bioRxiv paper;

 

"If distances were collected in bins the column 'distance' is replaced by two columns 'distbegin' and 'distend'..." (p.7).

 

However, when I tried using ds(), R gave me the error;

 

"Error in checkdata(data, region.table, sample.table, obs.table, formula) : Your data must (at least) have a column called 'distance'! "

 

I wonder if you could suggest what would appropriate in this situation, please? If I incorporate an extra column 'distance', should I make the values equal to the lower point of each bin (i.e. a duplicate of 'distbegin'), or would it be better to take the mid-point of each bin as a sort of pseudo distance measure?

 

Any guidance would be much appreciated.

 

Many thanks,

Tom

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Binned data in Distance for R
parts:
Hi Tom, hi listfolk,

Whoops, seems like that slipped past me (and the reviewers) and I didn't
implement that quite as I thought.

I have corrected this in the development version of Distance, which you
can load using:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/Distance")

Alternatively you can construct the distance column using:

data$distance <- data$distend - data$distbegin

this column is ignored anyway for a binned analysis but is required for
plotting. The patch I just wrote has Distance do the above step for you.

Sorry for the confusion and the mistake.

cheers,
--dave

to get the midpoint. Again, apologies for the confusion and my lack of
basic geometry knowledge (not enough coffee this morning it seems...)

cheers,
--dave
